ECE 6390 / RF links

dB & distance

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how logarithmic power units simplify a free-space link comparison.

A power level in dBW is 10 log₁₀(P/1 W); dBm uses 1 mW as its reference. Therefore PdBm = PdBW + 30. Negative logarithmic levels still represent positive physical power.

Power ratios use 10 log₁₀(P₂/P₁). Field-amplitude ratios use 20 log₁₀ only when the same impedance and power relation apply.

With fixed antenna gains and wavelength in a far-field free-space link, received power scales as 1/r². Changing distance from r₁ to r₂ changes received level by −20 log₁₀(r₂/r₁).

Example

One milliwatt is 0 dBm and −30 dBW. Doubling link distance reduces received power to one quarter, a 6.02 dB decrease under the stated assumptions.
